# BLO-35486 / BLO-38096 — order Job teardown so a run's Secrets outlive the pod that mounts them

Changed files: `src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts`,
`src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`. Landed across
[#2099](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2099) and
[#2116](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2116) (the latter's commits
are carried on this branch).

## The original defect ([BLO-35486](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-35486))

Every teardown path deleted the Job with `propagationPolicy: Background` — which
returns before the GC removes the pod — then deleted the per-run Secrets
immediately, so a pod still mid-image-pull started its container into
`secret "ac-<run>-env" not found`. Now: delete pods, poll until the API reports
none, delete the Job, then the Secrets; if a pod outlives the 60s budget neither
the Job nor the Secrets are deleted (deleting the Job reaps them via
`ownerReference`). This covers the `skipCleanup` and `retainJobs` paths, which
kept a pod alive on purpose and deleted its Secrets anyway. The keepalive
external-cancel path bypassed `cleanupJob()` entirely and is covered separately
by `teardownCancelledJob()`, which deliberately does *not* fail closed, because a
cancelled run only settles on a Job 404 and `completionTimeoutMs` may be 0.

Also raised the `podStartTimeoutSec` default 600 → 1800: a cold 3.3 GB
agent-image pull under 8-way contention measured 11m12s–12m36s, so the old budget
sat below the observed floor and failed the first wave of runs on every node
after each image bump.

## Secret ownership ahead of the launch-ack aborts (Ally review on #2099)

Moved the per-run Secrets' `ownerReference` patch above the two launch-ack abort
paths (no UID / no ack wired, and ack throws). Those paths run before the Job is
acknowledged, and since the change above they keep the Secrets when a pod
outlives teardown on the promise that Job GC collects them; with the patch still
below them the Secrets had no owner, and the adapter has no Secret reaper, so the
credential-bearing `<job>-env` Secret was orphaned for good. Also pinned the
concurrency guard's `{ waitForPods: false }` reap with a test: that loop sits
outside the 15s guard timeout, so dropping the opt-out would add up to 60s per
stale Job at every run start.

## Observability of the teardown poll (second Ally pass on #2099)

Log the first non-404 pod-list failure in `deleteJobPodsAndWait`, once. A
persistent RBAC/5xx on the teardown-confirmation poll retried silently to the
deadline and then failed closed on the same path as a genuinely wedged pod, so
the two were indistinguishable in a postmortem while both left the Job and
Secrets behind. Also recorded the `POD_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` invariant at its
declaration: it must exceed the pod's `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, which
`buildJobManifest` does not set (so pods ride the K8s 30s default), and the two
values live in different files — raising the grace period past 60s would make
every teardown hit the timeout and retain Job and Secrets with no reaper.

## 3-state teardown outcome ([BLO-38096](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-38096))

Split `deleteJobPodsAndWait`'s `boolean` into a `PodTeardownOutcome`
(`gone` / `alive` / `unobserved`). The single `false` conflated *pods are still
there* with *no pod list ever succeeded*, which cost two things. Both retention
warnings said "pod(s) … still present" in a branch where nothing had been seen —
the poll had failed to look. And `teardownCancelledJob`'s fail-open applied to
both, on a comment asserting "the pod delete has already been issued by that
point": false when one apiserver fault denies both verbs, because a non-404
`deleteCollection` failure is swallowed and falls through to the poll. It then
deleted the Job with the delete never issued and nothing observed, reaping the
run Secrets via `ownerReference` GC under a pod that can still start — the
original defect on the cancel path. The cancel path now fails open only on
`alive` (the apiserver answered, so the pod is Terminating) and closed on
`unobserved`; `cleanupJob` fails closed on both, unchanged. `unobserved` means
*no* poll ever succeeded, not *the last one failed*, so a late blip after clean
reads cannot flip a sound fail-open into the hang the fail-open exists to
prevent. Also made the `POD_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` cross-file invariant a test
rather than prose: `job-manifest.test.ts` now asserts the rendered pod spec
leaves `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` unset.

## `undeleted`: gate the fail-open on an accepted delete (Ally review on #2116)

Added a fourth outcome, `undeleted`, so the cancel path's fail-open is gated on
the pod delete actually being accepted rather than inferred from the poll.
`alive` was returned whenever a list succeeded, but `list` and `deletecollection`
are separate verbs: a Role granting pods `list` without `deletecollection`, or a
5xx on the delete alone, swallowed the delete failure, then saw the never-deleted
(not Terminating) pod and returned `alive`, and `teardownCancelledJob` deleted
the Job, so `ownerReference` GC reaped the run Secrets under a pod that could
still start. `deleteJobPodsAndWait` now records whether `deleteCollection` was
accepted and returns `alive` only then; a pod still listed after a refused delete
is `undeleted`, which `teardownCancelledJob` retains like `unobserved` and
`cleanupJob` retains like every non-`gone` outcome.

## Retry the refused delete each poll (two Ally findings on #2116 at `5b596d19`)

`deleteJobPodsAndWait` now re-issues the pod `deleteCollection` on every poll
until it is accepted, instead of once before the poll. Issued once, a single
transient fault (one 503) latched `undeleted` for the whole teardown,
indistinguishable from a persistent denial, and `teardownCancelledJob` retained
the Job over a pod that was never deleted and kept running. Now `undeleted` means
refused for the whole budget, as its doc claims, and a transient fault heals into
`alive`; the failure is still logged once, not per poll. Also documented the
pod-side cost of retaining on `undeleted`: deleting the Job with
`propagationPolicy: Background` hands pod removal to the
kube-controller-manager garbage collector, which acts under its own credentials,
so retaining gives up the last lever that stops the pod when this ServiceAccount
cannot — and the "needs a total read outage" justification applies to
`unobserved` only.

## Guard the teardown logs the cancel path has no catch above (Ally review at `a6ddd2b2`)

Guarded the two `await onLog(...)` calls inside `deleteJobPodsAndWait` with
`.catch(() => undefined)` — the last unguarded ones on the cancel path, which has
no supervision above it: the keepalive fires the teardown from a
`void (async () => {…})()` with no `.catch`, and `teardownCancelledJob` awaits
bare. A rejecting `onLog` therefore unwound past the outcome computation before
`deleteJobOnly` ran, so the Job was never deleted, `waitForJobCompletion` never
saw its 404, and the run hung — the exact hang the `alive` fail-open exists to
prevent, reached by the logging of the fault, with no warning line emitted
because the rejection *is* the log attempt. Both guards match the idiom
`teardownCancelledJob` already applies to its own two logs.

The delete failure is now reported **twice at most**: the first, which explains
why the retry started, and the final one at the deadline when the cause changed
(a 503 on poll 1 degrading into a persistent 403 reported the 503 while the
`undeleted` verdict was caused by the 403, so the logged cause and the cause of
the outcome disagreed). Emitted at the deadline rather than per poll, so a stable
error still logs once. And `cleanupJob`'s retention warning now names the
pod-side retain cost on the `undeleted` branch: `leaving Job and run Secrets for
K8s GC` reads as deferred cleanup, but on `undeleted` nothing was ever marked for
deletion, so the pod is not Terminating and keeps running until a later run's
concurrency guard reaps the Job. Five guards, each mutation-tested individually:
dropping any one `.catch`, suppressing the deadline line, or collapsing the
retain-cost clause turns the suite red on its own.

## Per-pod delete: the verb the Role actually grants (Ally C1/I2 on #2099 at `0dc2e567`)

Every section above describes the pod teardown as a `deleteCollection`. It never
worked. `deleteCollectionNamespacedPod` needs the `deletecollection` verb, which
`Role/paperclip-k8s-adapters` does not grant — measured 2026-10-06 with a
`SelfSubjectAccessReview` from `system:serviceaccount:paperclip:paperclip`
against a fake-subresource negative control (`deletecollection` false,
`delete` true, control false; `kubectl auth can-i` is subresource-blind on this
cluster, so the raw SSAR is the valid instrument). The call was therefore refused
on every poll, which lands in exactly the `undeleted` branch the previous two
sections built: **every** teardown retained, run Secrets never deleted, and the
cancel path never deleted the Job — so the cancelled run never settled. The
`undeleted` work was right; it was being reached unconditionally.

`deleteJobPodsAndWait` now lists first and deletes each returned pod by name with
`deleteNamespacedPod`, which needs only `delete`. Pods already carrying a
`deletionTimestamp`, and pods whose delete an earlier poll already accepted, are
skipped — that per-pod set is what the collection-wide `deleteAccepted` latch
used to do, so a refused delete still retries every poll and a transient fault
still heals into `alive`.

The 404-as-accepted branch is gone (Ally I2). On a collection delete a single 404
marked the whole teardown accepted and latched it, so one 404 suppressed every
later retry and turned a persistently refused delete into `alive` — which the
cancel path reads as licence to delete the Job. Per pod, a 404 means only that
that one pod is gone: it is not a refusal and it is not evidence about any other
pod. It can no longer fail open in either direction, because `gone` is still
returned only by a list that observed zero pods, never by anything the delete
call reports.

A pod list that never succeeds now never reaches a delete at all — there are no
names to delete — which is `unobserved` and fails closed on the same path as
before.

## Name the Secrets nothing will collect (Ally I3 on #2099 at `0dc2e567`)

The three `ownerReference` patches were copies of one block whose failures were
logged and dropped. A Secret whose patch did not land has no owner, so the Job GC
that eventually collects its siblings never reaches it, and the adapter has no
Secret reaper: it leaks silently, and it is the credential-bearing `<job>-env`
Secret that leaks. The three blocks are now one loop that records each failure
(and records all three when the Job returned no UID, where no patch is attempted
at all), and the retain path names the unowned Secrets in its warning. It does
not delete them — a pod that outlived teardown still mounts them, which is the
hazard this whole change exists to stop.

Four guards, each mutation-tested individually: reverting to a collection delete,
re-latching a 404 across the collection, treating a delete 404 as `gone`, or
dropping the unowned-Secret record each turns the suite red on its own. The first
pass of the two 404 tests passed against all three mutations — the fixtures built
the error as `{ code: 404 }` and `isK8s404` reads `response.statusCode` /
`statusCode` / the `HTTP-Code:` message, so the branch under test was never
entered. Mutation testing is what caught it; the tests asserted the right thing
and would have shipped as comments.

## The adopted Job reaches the same retain path (Ally I1 on #2099 at `746dd977`)

The previous increment hoisted the retention warning into `warnUnownedSecrets()`
and called it from both early aborts — but from inside their
`if (!adoptedExistingJob)` arm, so an *adopted* Job that aborted still retained
unowned Secrets with no log line. The same silent leak, one branch deeper.

Adoption is not a path where this cannot happen. It assigns `createdJobUid` from
the verdict, so the run reaches the `ownerReference` patch loop rather than the
no-UID skip, and a refused patch there fills `unownedSecrets` exactly as on the
created path. A 409 reattach still mints all three Secrets, because a
`createNamespacedSecret` 409 is absorbed into `replaceNamespacedSecret`. The net
effect was a credential-bearing `<job>-env` with no ownerReference, no reaper,
and no warning.

The review proposed hoisting the call above the `if`. That over-warns: on the
non-adopted path where `cleanupJob()` succeeds, `deleteRunSecrets()` does delete
them, so a warning there names Secrets that are gone. Folded the guard into the
cleanup condition instead — `!adoptedExistingJob && (await cleanupJob(...))`
short-circuits, so `cleanupJob()` is still never called on an adopted Job and the
"never tear down an adopted Job" invariant is untouched, while the `else` now
carries both cases that genuinely retain: pod-outlived, and adopted.

Mutation-tested: restoring the `if (!adoptedExistingJob)` wrapper at the
ack-throw abort alone reddens the new test on its warning assertion.

Two smaller findings from the same review. The per-Secret patch-failure log was
the last unguarded `await onLog` in the create phase; a rejection there unwound
out of `execute()` through the mutex `finally`, so the `unownedSecrets` entry
pushed one line earlier was discarded unread — the exact failure this increment
exists to make visible. And the teardown `finally` comment still read as an
unconditional description of its block after the emptiness test moved into the
helper.

## Rebase onto master: three reconciliations, not merges

149 commits of master landed under this branch. Three conflicts were places where
master's work and this branch's work had to be reconciled:

`PodWaitError` / `PodFailureKind` ([BLO-33503](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-33503))
already carries the init-container failure loop this branch re-added, so that
copy is dropped and only the unrecoverable-reason check is grafted into master's.
Both new throws are `PodWaitError` rather than bare `Error`: the sole consumer
labels an unclassified throw "Pod failure (unclassified)", so keeping the bare
`Error` would have been a quiet regression against the classification BLO-33503
had just added — invisible except in a postmortem.

Master gave each of the three `ownerReference` attaches an explicit
`setHeaderOptions("Content-Type", PatchStrategy.JsonPatch)` while this branch
collapsed the three into one loop. Both kept: one call site, with the header. Its
guard test pinned `toHaveLength(3)`, which is now 1 — re-pinned on the ratio
(every attach states its Content-Type), which is the invariant it was really
asserting and which does not re-break on the next refactor.

Master's `reports an unclassified label for a failure with no recorded kind`
rejects `listNamespacedPod` persistently, and this branch's teardown now polls
that same call to confirm the pods are gone, retrying to a 60s real-time deadline
before failing closed — past vitest's 5s cap. The test takes fake timers; the
retry is intended fail-closed behaviour and is unchanged.

## Rebuild onto master after BLO-32734 / BLO-39114 (2026-10-08)

#2099 was rebuilt onto master as a trailer-free replacement PR. Master had
rewritten `cleanupJob` in the meantime, so the merge was semantic, not textual:

- `cleanupJob` keeps master's export and its positional `reportMissingPodLog`
  (BLO-39114). The `opts.waitForPods` added here comes after it, and the
  boolean return is kept. The concurrency guard's foreign-Job reap passes all
  of it: the annotation path (validated by `isReapablePodLogPath`),
  `reportMissingPodLog`, and `waitForPods: false`.
- The pod-log reap stays unconditional (BLO-32734). It runs inside
  `deleteJobOnly`, after a separately caught Job delete, and also on the retain
  path when pods are not confirmed gone. The first merge attempt skipped it
  there on the assumption that the stale-Job guard would reap the log later.
  It would not: the guard only looks at non-terminal Jobs, a retained Job is
  normally already terminal, and `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` deletes it, leaking
  the log. A test now pins the retain-path reap.
- Every teardown log line goes through master's `logQuietly`, not
  `.catch(() => undefined)`. `.catch` would TypeError on a sink that returns
  no promise, and master's tests feed `cleanupJob` exactly that. The "Guard the
  teardown logs" section above describes the `.catch` form; read it as
  `logQuietly`.

Correction to that same section: the cancel path is not unsupervised.
`teardownCancelledJob` is awaited inside a `try` whose `catch` swallows the
error as a transient network failure. The hang it describes is still real, for
a different reason: `cancelled` is latched before the teardown, so the next
keepalive tick returns early instead of retrying.

## Close the three gaps in that rule (Ally I1–I3 on #2336 at `e93b1b1c`)

- `warnUnownedSecrets` and the ownerReference-patch warning still used
  `.catch(() => undefined)`. Both now go through `logQuietly`. A test feeds a
  sink that returns no promise down the patch-denied path; reverting either call
  site makes it fail.
- The `skipCleanup` and `retainJobs` branches of the teardown `finally` are now
  one retain branch with a reason string. Only `retainJobs` is reachable from the
  unit harness: no test drives `execute` through a full run. The new
  `retainJobs` test therefore pins `podsGone` staying false for both. Setting it
  true in the shared branch fails that test.
- The `cleanupJob pod-log reaping` suite now gives the list mock `{ items: [] }`
  explicitly. Before, the reset mock resolved `undefined`, which
  `podList?.items ?? []` reads as gone. With the explicit list, hardening that
  line to fail closed on an unparseable response leaves the suite green.

## `CreateContainerError` rides the deadline again; the alert that quotes 600s (Ally I1/I2 on #2336 at `861428d0`)

- `UNRECOVERABLE_WAITING_REASONS` no longer contains `CreateContainerError`. Its common causes, a reserved container name or a CRI `context deadline exceeded`, are node-local, and the kubelet clears them on its next sync. A run that one 2s poll would have seen Running must not fail on a single observation, so the reason rides the start deadline as it did before BLO-35486. Master threw on none of the three reasons. Two tests pin the change: `InvalidImageName` throws immediately, and a single `CreateContainerError` poll followed by `CreateContainerConfigError` fails on the second reason, not the first. Re-adding `CreateContainerError`, or dropping `InvalidImageName`, fails its test.
- The 1800s start deadline makes onprem-k8s `PaperclipAgentSchedulingFailureFleet` quote a wrong number, and its threshold was derived under 600s. The companion change is onprem-k8s branch `blo-35486-scheduling-alert-start-deadline`. It makes the Slack lead deploy-agnostic, states 1800 (600 before this deploys) in the body, and records a threshold re-check. Run error messages are retained only from 2026-09-24. Since then the only hours at >= 40 are the 2026-09-27 start-deadline wedge (227 and 74 events; a rolling 60m peak of 239). At a third of the rate that is still ~80/h, so the threshold stays at 40.
